title: A protocol for capturing RNA-sensing innate immune receptors in multiple conformations by single-particle cryo-EM
protocol: Mix RIG-I with 24-basepaired p3dsRNA at an 8:1 M ratio.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 12 hours.
Mix RIG-I with p2dsRNA at a 2:1 M ratio.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 12 hours.
Mix RIG-I with p1dsRNA at a 1.5:1 M ratio.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 12 hours.
Mix RIG-I with OHdsRNA at a 2:1 M ratio.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 12 hours.
Mix RIG-I with 30-basepaired p3SLR30 at a 1:1 M ratio.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 12 hours.
Mix RIG-I with OHSLR30 at a 1:1 M ratio.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 12 hours.
Load the 500 μL solution of each RIG-I:RNA complex to a Superdex 200 Increase 10/300 GL column with gel filtration buffer (without glycerol).
Concentrate the p3dsRNA:RIG-I complex to 0.3 mg/mL using an Amicon Ultra-0.5 centrifugal filter unit.
Concentrate the p2dsRNA:RIG-I complex to 1.5 mg/mL using an Amicon Ultra-0.5 centrifugal filter unit.
Concentrate the p1dsRNA:RIG-I complex to 0.4 mg/mL using an Amicon Ultra-0.5 centrifugal filter unit.
Concentrate the OHdsRNA:RIG-I complex to 1.5 mg/mL using an Amicon Ultra-0.5 centrifugal filter unit.
Concentrate the p3SLR30:RIG-I complex to 1.5 mg/mL using an Amicon Ultra-0.5 centrifugal filter unit.
Concentrate the OHSLR30:RIG-I complex to 1.5 mg/mL using an Amicon Ultra-0.5 centrifugal filter unit.
Concentrate the p3SLR30:RIG-I complex to 3.0 mg/mL.
Concentrate the OHSLR30:RIG-I complex to 2.5 mg/mL.
Incubate 20 μL of complex with 2.5 mM ATP/AMPPNP and 5 mM MgCl₂ on ice for 30 min before applying samples to the grids.
Mount the humidifier to Vitrobot Mark IV with O-ring well seated on top of the humidifier.
Add 50 mL distilled ddH2O to the humidifier.
Install two blot papers (Whatman no. 1) on each side.
Turn on the Vitrobot.
Set up the temperature to 22°C and the humidity to 100%.
Assemble the dry cryogen container with liquid nitrogen reservoir, float, brass cryogen cup, metal storage box holder, metal “spider legs,” and labeled grid boxes.
Cool the container by filling the reservoir with liquid nitrogen (LN2) but not adding to the brass cup.
Glow discharge the Quantifoil holey carbon R1.2/1.3 300 mesh Cu grids with carbon side facing up for 35 seconds at 25 mA using the PELCO easiGlow™ Glow Discharge Cleaning System.
Fill the brass cryogen cup with ethane when grids are ready for usage.
Close the valve of ethane after usage and pay attention to the ethane monitor.
Dispose used ethane in fume hood.
Hold one grid with Vitrobot tweezer and mount the tweezer to Vitrobot.
Lift the tweezer with grid, then transfer and lift the container.
Apply 3 μl samples to the carbon side of the grid.
Blot samples with force -4 for seconds (2, 3, 4, 5 s).
Plunge grid into liquid ethane.
Transfer the grid to one of the four slots of the grid box.
Repeat step with adjusted blotting time to freeze more grids.
Clip the frozen grids using the C-clip and the C-clip ring in the grid clipping station (ThermoFisher).
Store autogrids (clipped grids) in the autogrid boxes.
Transfer the autogrid boxes to the LN2 storage dewar for grid screening and data collection.
Mount the grids to the Glacios using the autoloader and screen the grids.
Take a full map of the grids using the software SerialEM.
Check the ice thickness on the grids.
Select grids with thin ice and pick 2–3 squares with ice of different thickness.
Select 2–3 holes in one square, take micrographs from either center or edge of the holes.
Check particle quality.
Check particle density.
Check ice thickness for suitability.
Evaluate crystalline ice contamination.
Collect micrographs from qualified grids.
Set up data collection conditions.
Ensure beam readiness for high-resolution data collection.
Collect micrographs with a calibrated pixel size of around 1 Å/pix and total electron exposure of 50–60 e-/Å² (total electron exposure/frame, 1–1.5 e-/Å²).
Use different defocus ranges during data acquisition.
For each stage movement, acquire one micrograph/hole on an R1.2/1.3 grid.
Collect approximately 3000 micrographs under super-resolution mode in one day.
Generate jpg pictures during data collection for monitoring image quality.
Estimate the CTF of selected micrographs with FFT box size of 1024 pixels.
Select the micrographs with resolution above 6 Å.
Manually evaluate the selected micrographs.
Dispose of micrographs with bad CTF fitness of Thon rings and ice contamination.
Pick up particles from selected micrographs using autopick.
Generate references for autopick.
Manually pick up 2,000–3,000 particles from 100 micrographs.
Adjust the scale and sigma of micrographs to help pick up particles.
Perform 2D classification with the manually picked particles using 10–20 classes.
Select the 2D classes showing features of complex.
Autopick particles from micrographs.
Optimize the “Picking threshold”, “Minimum inter-particle distance” and “Maximum stddev noise” (1, 100, 1.1).
Manually assess the autopick results.
Unpick the ice and carbon.
Perform 2D classification of the autopicked particles.
Downscale the particles by a factor of two using Extract job.
Perform 2D classification using 100 classes.
Select classes with features of particles.
Dispose of classes representing misfolded samples or ice contamination.
Carry out 2–3 rounds of 2D classification.
Select particles from all 2D classes containing a 1:1 RNA:RIG-I complex.
Select particles from 2D classes showing 1:2 RNA:RIG-I complex in top and bottom views.
Generate the initial model with selected binned particles.
Perform several rounds (2–3) of 3D classification through Relion.
Generate a single initial map using Relion 3D initial model settings.
Use the generated single initial map as the 3D reference for further 3D classification.
Select the best 3D class from multiple classifications.
Perform postprocessing job to yield maps at near-atomic global resolution.
Refine map resolutions ranging from 2.9 Å to 3.7 Å according to the FSC = 0.143 criterion.
Sharpen maps with B-factor.
